docs.title: vexy-overnight
docs.text:
vexy-overnight starts AI coding assistants (Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI) with fixed flags, and can hand a session that has just finished over to the next assistant, so that work continues without you typing the next command. It also keeps the instruction files those tools read (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md and others) identical across a project.

The package installs five commands:

Command Purpose vomgr Install the continuation hooks, switch them on and off, set preferences, sync instruction files, update the CLIs vocl Start Claude Code voco Start Codex voge Start Gemini CLI version-bump Tag the next patch version in a git repository and push it

docs.title: How continuation works, in one example
docs.text:
You have run vomgr install and vomgr enable claude. You start Claude in a project:

cd ~/work/my-app
vocl

When Claude finishes its turn and stops:

  1. Claude runs its Stop hook, which vomgr enable claude pointed at ~/.claude/hooks/vocl-go.py.
  2. vocl-go.py reads your preferences from ~/.vexy-overnight/settings.toml. By default, Claude hands over to Codex.
  3. It builds a prompt from the template for Claude, filling in up to five open - [ ] items from ~/work/my-app/TODO.md.
  4. It writes the Codex command line, the project directory and some environment variables to ~/.claude/hooks/vocl-new.json.
  5. It runs the terminal command configured for your platform (on macOS, by default, open -a Terminal …) and passes it a shell command that runs the helper vocl-new.py.
  6. The helper reads the JSON file, starts Codex in ~/work/my-app with the prompt and records the new process in ~/.vexy-overnight/session_state.json. If psutil is installed, it also stops the assistant process recorded there before.

Codex's notify hook works the same way and, by default, hands back to Claude.

The details are in How continuation works.

The assistants run without confirmations

vocl, voco, voge and the continuation commands start the assistants with their permission and sandbox checks turned off (--dangerously-skip-permissions, --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox --sandbox danger-full-access, -y). The assistant can then run any command and change any file without asking. Use them only in projects and on machines where that is acceptable.

docs.title: vomgr reference
docs.text: vomgr is built with Python Fire from the VomgrCLI class in src/vexy_overnight/cli.py. Run vomgr with no arguments to list the commands and groups.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Tool names are claude, codex and gemini, in any letter case. Any other name fails with tool must be one of claude, codex, gemini.
  • Flag names use underscores, as in the source: --backup_legacy, --self_update, --global_mode. Fire also accepts hyphens (--dry-run).
  • Boolean flags switch on by name: --check. Positional arguments can also be given by name: vomgr run claude equals vomgr run --tool=claude.
  • Commands return text or data; Fire prints it.
  • To see a command's flags without running it, write vomgr <command> -- --help.

docs.title: install
docs.text:
vomgr install [--backup_legacy] [--migrate]
  1. With --backup_legacy: back up ~/.claude/settings.json, ~/.codex/config.toml and ~/.gemini/config.json if they exist.
  2. Write the hook scripts into ~/.claude/hooks/, ~/.codex/ and ~/.gemini/. Existing copies are overwritten.
  3. With --migrate: replace hook commands that mention claude4ever.py or codex4ever.py with the new scripts. Without it: create ~/.claude/settings.json ({}) and ~/.codex/config.toml (empty) if they are missing.

Output: one line per step, ending with Installation complete.

docs.title: uninstall
docs.text:
vomgr uninstall

Delete the hook scripts and their pending JSON files, then remove the Claude Stop hook and the Codex notify entry. Output: Hooks removed and Configurations restored to defaults.

docs.title: enable, disable
docs.text:
vomgr enable claude      # set the Stop hook in ~/.claude/settings.json
vomgr enable codex       # set notify in ~/.codex/config.toml
vomgr disable claude     # remove the Stop hook
vomgr disable codex      # remove notify

enable replaces the whole Stop hook list or notify value. disable removes them, and also removes the hooks table when it becomes empty. For gemini, both print Gemini continuation not yet implemented.

Each change is written with a backup and a check: the file is copied to <name>.backup.<YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>, the new content is written to <name>.tmp, parsed again, and only then moved over the original. If any step fails, the backup is restored.

docs.title: status
docs.text:
vomgr status

Whether the Claude and Codex hooks point at the vexy-overnight scripts, and whether claude, codex and gemini are found on PATH.

docs.title: version
docs.text:
vomgr version

Print the package version.

docs.title: run
docs.text:
vomgr run claude [--cwd=DIR] [--model=NAME] [--prompt=TEXT]
vomgr run codex  [--cwd=DIR] [--profile=NAME] [--prompt=TEXT]
vomgr run gemini [--cwd=DIR] [--prompt=TEXT]

Start an assistant in the foreground and wait for it to exit. The commands it builds are the same as for vocl, voco and voge; see Launchers. --model applies to Claude only and --profile to Codex only. After the assistant exits, vomgr prints Launched <tool>.

If the assistant's command is not found, vomgr logs an install hint and exits with 1.

docs.title: rules
docs.text:
vomgr rules --sync
vomgr rules --append="Always run the tests before committing."
vomgr rules --search="ruff"
vomgr rules --replace='["old text", "new text"]'
vomgr rules --sync --global_mode
Flag Effect --sync Link all copies of each instruction file to the most recently changed one --append=TEXT Append TEXT to the most recent copy of each instruction file --search=TEXT Count lines containing TEXT in each instruction file --replace=[OLD, NEW] Replace OLD with NEW in every copy --global_mode Work on the assistants' home directories instead of the current directory

Flags can be combined; the actions run in the order of the table. With no action flag, the output is No rules action performed. See Instruction files for what each action does to the files.

docs.title: update
docs.text:
vomgr update --check
vomgr update --cli [--dry_run] [--skip='["llxprt", "qwen"]']
vomgr update --self_update [--dry_run]
vomgr update --all
Flag Effect --check Print tool: current -> available for claude, codex, gemini and vexy-overnight --cli Update the assistant CLIs (see below) --self_update Upgrade the vexy-overnight package --all --cli and --self_update --dry_run Log what would run, change nothing --skip List of tool names to leave out of --cli

--cli runs npm install -g for each of these packages, then brew update and brew upgrade codex:

Name npm package claude @anthropic-ai/claude-code@latest gemini @google/gemini-cli@nightly llxprt @vybestack/llxprt-code@nightly qwen @qwen-code/qwen-code@nightly terragon @terragon-labs/cli@latest justevery @just-every/code@latest

--self_update runs uv pip install --upgrade vexy-overnight if uv is on PATH, otherwise python -m pip install --upgrade vexy-overnight with the Python that runs vomgr.

The before and after versions of an update are appended to ~/.vexy-overnight/update.log.

--check reports available as latest for Claude and nightly for Gemini; it does not look these up. For Codex it asks Homebrew; for vexy-overnight, PyPI.

docs.title: Preference groups
docs.text: These groups read and write ~/.vexy-overnight/settings.toml. See Configuration for the file format.

docs.title: continuation
docs.text:
vomgr continuation status
vomgr continuation set claude codex     # when claude stops, start codex
vomgr continuation disable codex        # codex hands over to nobody

set also switches the source on. Output: claude continuation now targets codex.

docs.title: prompt
docs.text:
vomgr prompt show claude
vomgr prompt set claude $'Carry on with:\n{todo}'

The shell must pass a real line break: $'…' does that in Bash and Zsh. In plain double quotes, \n is stored as a backslash and an n.

The template for a tool is used when that tool finishes. Placeholders: {todo}, {plan}, {target}, {source}; see How continuation works.

docs.title: notify
docs.text:
vomgr notify show
vomgr notify set --message="Handing over to {target}" --enabled=True
vomgr notify sound Glass

When enabled, the helper prints [vomgr] <message> after it starts the next assistant. {target} and {source} are filled in. The sound name is stored and passed on in VOMGR_NOTIFICATION_SOUND, but nothing plays it in this version.

docs.title: terminal
docs.text:
vomgr terminal show darwin

open
-a
Terminal
--args
bash
-lc
{command}; exec bash

The command used to open a terminal for the helper, per platform (darwin, linux, windows). {command} is replaced by cd <project> && <python> <helper script>. show fails with no terminal command configured for <platform> when there is none.

vomgr terminal set <platform> <arg> … stores a new command; the last argument must contain {command}. Fire reads any argument that starts with - as a flag, so commands such as bash -lc "{command}" cannot be entered this way: the call fails. Edit [terminals.defaults] in ~/.vexy-overnight/settings.toml instead; see Configuration.

docs.title: Where things are stored
docs.text:
Path Written by Content ~/.vexy-overnight/settings.toml vomgr continuation, prompt, notify, terminal; created with defaults by the first command or hook that reads it Your preferences ~/.vexy-overnight/settings.toml.backup.<timestamp> every save of the preferences The previous version ~/.vexy-overnight/session_state.json the helper scripts The assistant process started last ~/.vexy-overnight/update.log vomgr update Versions before and after updates ~/.claude/settings.json vomgr enable/disable claude, install, uninstall Claude Code settings, including the Stop hook ~/.codex/config.toml vomgr enable/disable codex, install, uninstall Codex settings, including notify <file>.backup.<YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS> every change to the two files above The previous version

Backups are never deleted by vomgr. Remove old ones by hand.

docs.title: settings.toml
docs.text:
Every key is optional. Missing keys take the defaults shown here, which is also what a new file contains:

kill_old_sessions = true

[continuations.claude]
enabled = true
target = "codex"

[continuations.codex]
enabled = true
target = "claude"

[continuations.gemini]
enabled = false
target = "claude"

[prompts]
claude = "Continue work in the next tool. Outstanding tasks:\n{todo}"
codex = "Pick up the session with these TODOs:\n{todo}"
gemini = "Continue assisting with current plan:\n{plan}"

[notifications]
enabled = true
message = "Continuing on {target}"
sound = "success"

[terminals.defaults]
darwin = ["open", "-a", "Terminal", "--args", "bash", "-lc", "{command}; exec bash"]
windows = ["wt", "powershell", "-NoExit", "-Command", "{command}"]
linux = ["gnome-terminal", "--", "bash", "-lc", "{command}; exec bash"]

[terminals.per_tool]

When the file is read, a target that is not claude, codex or gemini, or a kill_old_sessions that is not a boolean, raises an error. The vomgr command then fails; a hook falls back to the built-in defaults.

docs.title: continuations
docs.text:
One table per tool that can stop. enabled switches handover on for that tool; target names the tool to start next. A tool can target itself.

Commands: vomgr continuation set <source> <target>, vomgr continuation disable <source>, vomgr continuation status.

Turning a tool off here leaves its hook registered with the assistant. The hook still runs, sees the setting and exits. To unregister the hook, use vomgr disable <tool>.

docs.title: prompts
docs.text:
One template per tool. The template of the tool that stopped is used. Placeholders are {todo}, {plan}, {target} and {source}; see How continuation works.

Commands: vomgr prompt set <tool> <template>, vomgr prompt show <tool>.

docs.title: notifications
docs.text:
enabled and message control the line [vomgr] <message> that the helper prints after it starts the next assistant; {target} and {source} are filled in. sound is stored and passed to the next assistant in VOMGR_NOTIFICATION_SOUND; nothing plays it in this version.

Commands: vomgr notify set --message=… --enabled=…, vomgr notify sound <name>, vomgr notify show.

docs.title: terminals
docs.text:
The command that opens a terminal for the helper. {command} is replaced by cd <project> && <python> <helper script>, with each part shell-quoted. The platform key is platform.system() in lower case: darwin, linux or windows.

terminals.per_tool lets one target tool use a different terminal. Its keys are tool names, and each holds platform keys:

[terminals.per_tool.codex]
linux = ["xterm", "-e", "bash", "-lc", "{command}; exec bash"]

Look-up order: per_tool.<target>.<platform>, then defaults.<platform>, then the built-in fallback described in How continuation works.

Edit this section of the file directly. vomgr terminal set cannot store commands with arguments that start with -; see vomgr reference.

docs.title: kill_old_sessions
docs.text: With true, the helper stops the previously recorded assistant process after it starts the new one. This needs psutil.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
These are read by the hook scripts:

Variable Effect VOMGR_HOOK_FORCE_DIRECT 1 runs the helper in the hook's process instead of a new terminal. Useful for debugging. VOMGR_TERMINAL_APP macOS application used by the osascript fallback when no terminal command is configured. Default Terminal. CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR Set by Claude Code; the Claude hook uses it as the project directory. PWD Last-resort project directory for both hooks.

The helpers set these for the next assistant: VOMGR_TARGET_TOOL, VOMGR_SOURCE_TOOL, VOMGR_PROMPT, VOMGR_PROJECT_DIR, VOMGR_NOTIFICATION_ENABLED, VOMGR_NOTIFICATION_MESSAGE, VOMGR_NOTIFICATION_SOUND, VOMGR_KILL_OLD.

docs.title: How continuation works
docs.text:
Continuation is a chain of small steps, each in its own file. Knowing the chain makes it easy to see where something stopped.

assistant stops
  → its hook runs           (~/.claude/hooks/vocl-go.py or ~/.codex/voco-go.py)
  → hook writes a job file  (vocl-new.json or voco-new.json, next to the hook)
  → hook opens a terminal   (command from settings.toml)
  → helper runs             (vocl-new.py or voco-new.py)
  → helper starts the next assistant and records it

docs.title: 1. The assistant calls the hook
docs.text:
vomgr enable registers the hooks:

Assistant Where What is registered Claude Code ~/.claude/settings.json, hooks.Stop "~/.claude/hooks/vocl-go.py" "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR" Codex ~/.codex/config.toml, notify ~/.codex/voco-go.py

Claude runs its Stop hook when it finishes responding. Codex runs its notify program on its notification events.

The hook scripts start with #!/usr/bin/env python3 and import vexy_overnight.hook_runtime, so the python3 on PATH must have the package installed.

docs.title: 2. The hook finds the project directory
docs.text:
The Claude hook takes the first of these that exists:

  1. The directory in $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR.
  2. project_dir or cwd from the JSON that Claude sends on standard input.
  3. $PWD, or the current directory.

The Codex hook takes the first of these that exists:

  1. cwd or working_directory from the context field of the JSON payload.
  2. cwd from the payload.
  3. The cwd recorded in the most recently changed ~/.codex/sessions/*.jsonl file.
  4. $PWD, or the current directory.

docs.title: 3. The hook reads the preferences
docs.text:
From ~/.vexy-overnight/settings.toml (created with defaults if missing; see Configuration):

  • If continuation is off for the tool that just stopped, the hook deletes any pending job file and exits. Nothing else happens.
  • Otherwise it reads the target tool. A target other than claude, codex or gemini is treated as claude.

docs.title: 4. The prompt
docs.text:
The hook takes the prompt template of the tool that just stopped and fills in:

Placeholder Value {todo} Up to five lines of <project>/TODO.md that start with - [ ], or No open TODO items. {plan} The first five non-empty lines of <project>/PLAN.md, or No plan summary available. {target} The tool that will start next {source} The tool that just stopped

If the template contains another {…} placeholder, the template is used as it is, without any substitution.

Example: with the template Carry on with:\n{todo} and this TODO.md:

- [ ] First task
- [x] Done task
- [ ] Second task

the prompt is:

Carry on with:
- [ ] First task
- [ ] Second task

docs.title: 5. The command for the next assistant
docs.text:
Target Command claude claude --continue --dangerously-skip-permissions --prompt "<prompt>" codex codex --cd=<project> -m gpt5 --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox --sandbox danger-full-access "<prompt>" gemini gemini -c -y "<prompt>"

The executable is resolved with which; if that fails, the bare name is used.

docs.title: 6. The job file
docs.text:
The hook writes the command, the project directory and a set of environment variables to a JSON file next to itself: ~/.claude/hooks/vocl-new.json or ~/.codex/voco-new.json. A real example, with paths shortened:

{
  "command": [
    "…/bin/codex",
    "--cd=…/proj",
    "-m",
    "gpt5",
    "--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox",
    "--sandbox",
    "danger-full-access",
    "Carry on with:\n- [ ] First task\n- [ ] Second task"
  ],
  "cwd": "…/proj",
  "env": {
    "VOMGR_TARGET_TOOL": "codex",
    "VOMGR_SOURCE_TOOL": "claude",
    "VOMGR_PROMPT": "Carry on with:\n- [ ] First task\n- [ ] Second task",
    "VOMGR_PROJECT_DIR": "…/proj",
    "VOMGR_NOTIFICATION_ENABLED": "1",
    "VOMGR_NOTIFICATION_MESSAGE": "Handing over to codex",
    "VOMGR_NOTIFICATION_SOUND": "Glass",
    "VOMGR_KILL_OLD": "1"
  }
}

The next assistant gets these variables in its environment.

docs.title: 7. The terminal
docs.text:
The hook then starts the helper script (vocl-new.py or voco-new.py) in a new terminal:

  1. If VOMGR_HOOK_FORCE_DIRECT=1 is set, it runs the helper directly in the hook's own process and skips the terminal.
  2. Otherwise it takes the terminal command for the target tool and platform from the preferences (terminals.per_tool, then terminals.defaults), replaces {command} with cd <project> && <python> <helper> and starts it without waiting.
  3. If no command is configured for the platform: on macOS it asks the application named in $VOMGR_TERMINAL_APP (default Terminal) to run the command through osascript; on Windows it opens cmd.exe; elsewhere it runs the helper directly.

If the helper script is missing, the hook prints Helper script … is missing. Re-run vomgr install. and exits with 1.

docs.title: 8. The helper starts the next assistant
docs.text:
The helper:

  1. Reads the job file. If it is missing or invalid, it prints a message and stops.
  2. Starts the command in the project directory, with the variables from env added to its environment.
  3. If VOMGR_KILL_OLD is 1 and ~/.vexy-overnight/session_state.json records an earlier session, stops that process: it sends a terminate signal, waits up to five seconds, then kills it. It only does this when psutil is installed and the process name contains claude, codex or gemini.

  4. Records the new process in ~/.vexy-overnight/session_state.json:

    {
  "tool": "codex",
  "pid": 51976,
  "start_time": "2026-10-12T23:06:51.040162",
  "cwd": "…/proj"
}

  5. If notifications are on, prints [vomgr] <message>.

  6. Waits for the assistant to exit.

docs.title: Gemini
docs.text: ~/.gemini/voge-go.py is a placeholder. It prints Gemini continuation not yet implemented. Check for updates. and exits. vomgr enable gemini registers nothing. Gemini can still be a target: another tool can hand over to it.

docs.title: Repository layout
docs.text:
Path Content src/vexy_overnight/cli.py VomgrCLI and the preference groups behind vomgr src/vexy_overnight/config.py ConfigManager: edits ~/.claude/settings.json and ~/.codex/config.toml with backup and rollback src/vexy_overnight/hooks.py HookManager: renders the hook templates into the home directory src/vexy_overnight/hooks_tpl/ Templates for vocl-go.py, vocl-new.py, voco-go.py, voco-new.py, voge-go.py src/vexy_overnight/hook_runtime.py Code shared by the rendered hooks: prompt, command, terminal, launch src/vexy_overnight/user_settings.py Reads and writes ~/.vexy-overnight/settings.toml src/vexy_overnight/session_state.py Records and stops assistant sessions src/vexy_overnight/launchers.py LauncherManager, vocl, voco, voge src/vexy_overnight/rules.py RulesManager for instruction files src/vexy_overnight/updater.py UpdateManager for vomgr update src/vexy_overnight/tools/version_bump.py version-bump src/vexy_overnight/vexy_overnight.py Config, Summary and process_data, kept for compatibility with early releases tests/ pytest suite src_docs/ Documentation source (this site)

The hook templates are rendered with Python's str.format. Literal braces in a template must be doubled, which is why the templates write dict() instead of {}.

docs.title: Set up an environment
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-overnight.git
cd vexy-overnight
uv sync --extra test

docs.title: Run the tests
docs.text:
uv run --extra test python -m pytest -q -o addopts=""

The tests that touch the home directory replace HOME with a temporary directory, and the hook tests use stub claude and codex executables, so no real assistant is started.

On the current main branch, with psutil added (uv run --extra test --with psutil …), 91 tests passed and two failed: test_vocl_go_when_todo_items_present_then_prompt_includes_unfinished and test_voco_go_when_context_string_then_uses_context_directory; in both, the stub assistant did not record its arguments. Without psutil, five more tests in tests/test_session_state.py fail on the missing module.

docs.title: Lint and format
docs.text:
uvx ruff check src tests
uvx ruff format --respect-gitignore src tests

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text: The version comes from git tags (vX.Y.Z) through hatch-vcs. At build time it is written to src/vexy_overnight/__version__.py, which is not tracked in git. Between tags the version looks like 1.1.3.dev0+gffd58a9cc. In a source checkout that was never built or installed, vexy_overnight.__version__ falls back to the installed distribution's metadata, then to 0.0.0.

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
./build.sh            # docs and package
./build.sh docs       # src_docs/ → docs/
./build.sh package    # dist/*.whl and dist/*.tar.gz, checked with twine

The wheel contains the package, including py.typed and the hooks_tpl/ templates. The source distribution adds tests/, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, DEPENDENCIES.md, LICENSE and pyproject.toml.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
src_docs/build.sh          # strict build into docs/
src_docs/build.sh serve    # live preview on http://127.0.0.1:8000

Sources are in src_docs/md/, the configuration in src_docs/mkdocs.yml. The Docs workflow rebuilds docs/ on each push to main that touches src_docs/.

docs.title: Release
docs.text:
1. Export a PyPI token for uv publish, for example UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN.

  2. Run:

    ./publish.sh

    gitnextver commits pending changes, tags the next vX.Y.Z and pushes. The script then builds from that tag and uploads with uv publish.

The pushed tag also triggers the Release workflow, which builds the package, uploads it to PyPI with skip-existing and creates a GitHub release.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.10 or newer (requires-python = ">=3.10").
  • macOS or Linux. The hooks call which, and the default terminal commands use Terminal.app on macOS and gnome-terminal on Linux. A Windows terminal command is defined but untested here.
  • At least one of the assistants you want to drive:
    • Claude Code: npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
    • Codex: brew install codex
    • Gemini CLI: npm install -g @google/gemini-cli

The Python dependencies are loguru, fire, rich, tomli and tomli-w. psutil is optional: without it, the previous assistant process is not stopped when a new one takes over.

docs.title: Install the package
docs.text:
The hook scripts that vomgr install writes run with #!/usr/bin/env python3 and import vexy_overnight. The one requirement is that the python3 on your PATH can import the package. The commands below are common ways to get there; they were not tested for this page, and on a Python managed by Homebrew or the operating system, pip install --user and uv pip install --system can refuse with an externally-managed-environment error (PEP 668). In that case use a Python you control, for example one installed with uv python install or pyenv, and put it first on your PATH.

pip (user install)uv into the system Pythonuv tool (commands only) 
python3 -m pip install --user vexy-overnight

uv pip install --system vexy-overnight

uv tool install vexy-overnight

This puts vomgr, vocl, voco, voge and version-bump on your PATH, but in an isolated environment. The hook scripts then cannot import vexy_overnight unless that environment's Python is the python3 on your PATH. Use one of the other two methods if you want continuation.

Check the installation:

vomgr version
python3 -c "import vexy_overnight; print(vexy_overnight.__version__)"

Both commands print the same version, for example 1.1.2.

docs.title: Install the hooks
docs.text:
vomgr install

This writes the hook scripts and makes sure the assistants' config files exist:

File Content ~/.claude/hooks/vocl-go.py Claude Stop hook ~/.claude/hooks/vocl-new.py Helper that starts the next assistant ~/.codex/voco-go.py Codex notify hook ~/.codex/voco-new.py Helper that starts the next assistant ~/.gemini/voge-go.py Placeholder that prints Gemini continuation not yet implemented. Check for updates. ~/.claude/settings.json Created as {} if missing ~/.codex/config.toml Created empty if missing

vomgr install does not switch continuation on. That is vomgr enable; see Quick start.

Options:

  • --backup_legacy copies ~/.claude/settings.json, ~/.codex/config.toml and ~/.gemini/config.json to <name>.backup.<YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS> first.
  • --migrate rewrites hooks that point at the older claude4ever.py and codex4ever.py scripts so they point at vocl-go.py and voco-go.py, instead of creating empty config files.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
1. Remove the hooks and the hook entries from the assistants' configs:

    vomgr uninstall

    This deletes the files in the table above (except settings.json and config.toml), removes the Stop hook from ~/.claude/settings.json and the notify entry from ~/.codex/config.toml.

  2. Remove the package with the tool you installed it with, for example python3 -m pip uninstall vexy-overnight.

  3. Optionally delete ~/.vexy-overnight/, which holds your preferences, the session record and the update log.

docs.title: vocl, voco, voge
docs.text:
The three launchers find the assistant's executable, build a fixed command line and run it in the foreground. They are thin wrappers: they do not read ~/.vexy-overnight/settings.toml, and they do not install or check hooks.

The executable is looked up with which, then in /usr/local/bin, ~/.local/bin and /opt/homebrew/bin. If it is not found, the launcher logs an install hint and exits with 1:

Launcher Hint vocl npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code voco brew install codex voge npm install -g @google/gemini-cli

Warning

All three launchers turn off the assistant's permission or sandbox checks. Review the command lines below before you use them.

docs.title: vocl
docs.text:
vocl [WORDS…]

Runs:

claude --dangerously-skip-permissions --model claude-sonnet-4 [--prompt "WORDS…"]

All arguments are joined with spaces into one prompt. vocl has no options of its own; something like vocl --help becomes the prompt --help.

vomgr run claude --model=NAME replaces claude-sonnet-4 with NAME. vomgr run claude --cwd=DIR changes to DIR first.

docs.title: voco
docs.text:
voco [-m NAME] [-p | -e] [WORDS…]

Runs:

codex -m NAME [-p -e] --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox --sandbox danger-full-access [WORDS…]
Argument Effect -m NAME Passed to codex as -m NAME. Default: gpt5. -p or -e Adds -p -e to the codex command line anything else Joined with spaces into the prompt, passed as the last argument

vomgr run codex --cwd=DIR --profile=NAME passes --cd=DIR and -m NAME.

docs.title: voge
docs.text:
voge [WORDS…]

Runs:

gemini -c -y [WORDS…]

All arguments are joined into one prompt. vomgr run gemini --cwd=DIR changes to DIR first.

docs.title: version-bump
docs.text:
version-bump tags the next patch version of the git repository in the current directory and pushes it.

version-bump [-v | --verbose]

It does this, in order, and stops with exit code 1 at the first failure:

  1. Checks that .git exists in the current directory. Otherwise: Error: Not a git repository.
  2. Checks that git status --porcelain is empty. Otherwise: Error: Working tree not clean. Please commit changes first.
  3. Runs git pull.
  4. Lists tags matching v*.*.*, takes the highest by number and adds one to the patch number. With no such tags, the version is v1.0.0.
  5. Prints Creating version: vX.Y.Z and runs git tag vX.Y.Z.
  6. Runs git push and git push --tags.
  7. Prints ✅ Successfully created and pushed vX.Y.Z.

Example: with tags v1.0.9 and v1.0.10, the next tag is v1.0.11, because the comparison is numeric.

--verbose prints each step and shows the output of the git commands.

Note

version-bump only creates and pushes a tag. It does not change any file, build a package or upload anything. In this repository, pushing a v* tag starts the release workflow.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text: This page sets up continuation from Claude Code to Codex and back, checks the setup, and starts a session.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• vexy-overnight is installed so that python3 can import it. See Installation.
  • claude and codex are installed and logged in.
  • You have read the warning on the home page: the assistants run without permission prompts.

docs.title: 1. Install the hooks
docs.text:
vomgr install

Continuation hooks installed
Configuration files set up
Installation complete

The hook scripts are now in ~/.claude/hooks/ and ~/.codex/. Nothing calls them yet.

docs.title: 2. Connect the hooks to the assistants
docs.text:
vomgr enable claude
vomgr enable codex

claude continuation enabled
codex continuation enabled

What changed:

  • ~/.claude/settings.json now has a Stop hook that runs "~/.claude/hooks/vocl-go.py" "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR". Any other Stop hooks in that file are replaced.
  • ~/.codex/config.toml now has notify = ["~/.codex/voco-go.py"] (with your real home path). Any previous notify value is replaced.

Before each change, the file is copied to <name>.backup.<YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS> next to it.

docs.title: 3. Check the status
docs.text:
vomgr status

vomgr status
Claude: enabled (installed=True)
Codex: enabled (installed=True)
Gemini installed=True

installed tells whether the command is found on your PATH.

docs.title: 4. Check where each tool hands over
docs.text:
vomgr continuation status

The first time you run a command that reads preferences, ~/.vexy-overnight/settings.toml is created with the defaults: Claude hands over to Codex, Codex hands over to Claude, Gemini does not hand over.

claude: {"enabled": true, "target": "codex"}
codex:  {"enabled": true, "target": "claude"}
gemini: {"enabled": false, "target": "claude"}

To make Claude continue in Claude instead:

vomgr continuation set claude claude

docs.title: 5. Give the next session something to do
docs.text:
The prompt for the next assistant is built from the template for the tool that just finished. The default Claude template is:

Continue work in the next tool. Outstanding tasks:
{todo}

{todo} becomes the first five lines of TODO.md in the project directory that start with - [ ], or No open TODO items. if there are none. Keep a TODO.md with open items:

- [ ] Add input validation to the upload form
- [ ] Write tests for the CSV exporter

docs.title: 6. Start working
docs.text:
cd ~/work/my-app
vocl

vocl starts Claude with --dangerously-skip-permissions --model claude-sonnet-4. When Claude stops, the Stop hook prepares the Codex command and opens a terminal that runs it. When Codex finishes, its notify hook does the same in the other direction.

docs.title: Stop the loop
docs.text:
To stop handing over without removing anything:

vomgr continuation disable claude
vomgr continuation disable codex

The hooks still run, but they exit at once and delete their pending vocl-new.json or voco-new.json.

To disconnect the hooks from the assistants completely:

vomgr disable claude
vomgr disable codex

docs.title: Instruction files
docs.text: Each AI assistant reads its own instruction file: Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md, Codex reads AGENTS.md, Gemini CLI reads GEMINI.md, and so on. When a project keeps several of them, they drift apart. vomgr rules finds them, links them together and edits them in one go.

docs.title: Which files
docs.text:
vomgr rules works on files with these exact names:

  • CLAUDE.md
  • AGENTS.md
  • GEMINI.md
  • QWEN.md
  • LLXPRT.md
  • .cursorrules

docs.title: Where it looks
docs.text:
Mode Searched recursively Default The current directory --global_mode ~/.claude, ~/.codex, ~/.gemini, ~/.qwen, ~/.llxprt, ~/.cursor (those that exist)

When fd is installed, the search runs fd -t f <name> <dir>. fd skips hidden files and directories and anything listed in .gitignore, so .cursorrules is not found in that case. It also reads the name as a regular expression, so a file such as OLD_CLAUDE.md matches CLAUDE.md too. Without fd, the search uses Python's recursive glob, which matches the exact name, including hidden files.

Files are grouped by name: all CLAUDE.md files in one group, all AGENTS.md files in another.

docs.title: --sync
docs.text:
vomgr rules --sync

For each name with two or more copies:

  1. Pick the "parent": the non-empty copy with the most recent modification time.
  2. Replace every other copy with a hard link to the parent. If a hard link fails (for example across file systems), use a symbolic link.

After syncing, editing any copy edits all of them.

Warning

--sync deletes the other copies before linking them. Their content is lost unless it is in version control. It links files of the same name only: CLAUDE.md files are linked to each other, not to AGENTS.md.

Example: a repository with CLAUDE.md at the root and an older docs/CLAUDE.md:

./CLAUDE.md        modified today       ← parent
./docs/CLAUDE.md   modified last week   → replaced by a link to ./CLAUDE.md

docs.title: --append
docs.text:
vomgr rules --append="Run the tests before every commit."

For each name, append a blank line, the text and a newline to the parent copy. Copies that are linked to it show the change too; copies that are not linked do not change.

docs.title: --search
docs.text:
vomgr rules --search="pytest"

CLAUDE.md: 3 match(es)
AGENTS.md: 3 match(es)

Counts lines that contain the text, exactly as typed (case-sensitive, no patterns). Linked copies are counted once. With no match: No matches found.

docs.title: --replace
docs.text:
vomgr rules --replace='["uvx hatch test", "uv run pytest"]'

Replace every occurrence of the first string with the second, in every copy. Linked copies are written once. The value must be a list of exactly two strings, otherwise: replace expects two values: search and replace.

docs.title: Combining actions
docs.text:
Several flags can be given in one call. They run in this order: sync, append, search, replace.

vomgr rules --sync --append="See TODO.md for open work."

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Start with:

vomgr status                 # are the hooks registered? are the CLIs on PATH?
vomgr continuation status    # which tool hands over to which?
ls ~/.claude/hooks ~/.codex  # are the hook scripts there?

docs.title: Nothing happens when the assistant stops
docs.text:
Work through the chain in How continuation works from the top.

  1. Hook registered? vomgr status must say enabled for the tool. If not, run vomgr enable <tool>.
  2. Hook scripts present? ~/.claude/hooks/vocl-go.py and vocl-new.py, or ~/.codex/voco-go.py and voco-new.py. If not, run vomgr install.
  3. Continuation on? vomgr continuation status must show "enabled": true for the tool that stopped. If it is off, the hook exits silently.

  4. Can the hook import the package? Run the same Python the hook uses:

    python3 -c "import vexy_overnight.hook_runtime"

    A ModuleNotFoundError means the package is installed in a different environment, for example with uv tool install. Install it for this python3; see Installation.

  5. Does the hook run at all? Run it by hand, with the terminal step turned off:

    cd ~/work/my-app
CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$PWD" VOMGR_HOOK_FORCE_DIRECT=1 ~/.claude/hooks/vocl-go.py < /dev/null

    This starts the next assistant in the current terminal. Errors are printed.

  6. Job file written? After the hook runs, ~/.claude/hooks/vocl-new.json (or ~/.codex/voco-new.json) should hold the command. Check the command and cwd fields.

docs.title: A terminal window opens, but the assistant does not start
docs.text:
The terminal command did not run the helper. On macOS the default is open -a Terminal --args bash -lc "{command}; exec bash". Test the helper on its own:

python3 ~/.claude/hooks/vocl-new.py

If that works, change the terminal command in ~/.vexy-overnight/settings.toml; see Configuration. Remove the entry for your platform from [terminals.defaults] to use the osascript fallback, which runs the command in a new window of the app named in $VOMGR_TERMINAL_APP (default Terminal).

docs.title: Helper script … is missing. Re-run vomgr install.
docs.text: The hook found no helper next to it. Run vomgr install.

docs.title: The next assistant starts in the wrong directory
docs.text: The hook uses $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR (Claude) or the payload and the latest Codex session file (Codex) to find the project, and falls back to $PWD. See How continuation works. Check the cwd field in the job file.

docs.title: The prompt says No open TODO items.
docs.text: {todo} reads TODO.md in the project directory and keeps only lines that start with - [ ] (leading spaces are ignored). Lines such as * [ ] task or - [x] task do not count. Only the first five are used.

docs.title: The previous assistant keeps running
docs.text:
Stopping the previous session needs psutil:

python3 -m pip install --user psutil

It also needs kill_old_sessions = true in the preferences, and a process name that contains claude, codex or gemini.

docs.title: My other Claude Stop hooks are gone
docs.text: vomgr enable claude replaces the whole hooks.Stop list in ~/.claude/settings.json, and vomgr disable claude removes it. Restore the earlier version from ~/.claude/settings.json.backup.<timestamp> and add the vocl-go.py entry by hand next to your other hooks. The same applies to notify in ~/.codex/config.toml.

docs.title: tool must be one of claude, codex, gemini
docs.text: A command got a tool name it does not know. Use claude, codex or gemini.

docs.title: vomgr terminal set fails
docs.text: Fire reads arguments that start with - as its own flags. Edit [terminals.defaults] in ~/.vexy-overnight/settings.toml instead.

docs.title: vomgr update --check shows unknown for vexy-overnight
docs.text: The version check for the package itself fails in this version and reports unknown. Use vomgr version and compare it with PyPI yourself.

docs.title: Gemini continuation not yet implemented
docs.text: That is the current state. Gemini can be a target, but it cannot hand over to another tool.

docs.title: A vocl argument is treated as a prompt
docs.text: vocl and voge turn all their arguments into the prompt; they have no options. vocl --help starts Claude with the prompt --help. Use vomgr run claude --model=… to pass a model.
